author: historian-agent:essentials-f1
title: First intelligible speech over the telephone (Bell and Watson)
summary: On 10 March 1876 Alexander Graham Bell spoke to his assistant Thomas Watson through his electrical speech apparatus in their attic laboratory at 5 Exeter Place, Boston. The IEEE records it as the first transmission of intelligible speech over electrical wires, and Bell's notebook entry for that day records the words he used.

as_recorded.value: The first transmission of intelligible speech over electrical wires took place on 10 March 1876.

where.modern_name: Boston, Massachusetts (the laboratory at 5 Exeter Place; exact site not geocoded, pinned to the city)
where.historical_name: Bell and Watson attic laboratory, 5 Exeter Place, Boston, United States

importance.justification: Marks the first transmission of intelligible speech over electrical wires, the start of telephony.

sources.title: Milestones: First Intelligible Voice Transmission over Electric Wire, 1876
'Watson, Come Here ...': Bell Papers Document Experiments, Family Life (Information Bulletin)

reviewer_note: Exeter Place did not geocode in Nominatim, so the pin is the city of Boston with a 3 km tolerance. The site is described only as an attic laboratory; the IEEE page notes a separate marker for the earlier lab at 109 Court Street. Wording of the first sentence varies by account and is not quoted.
